unmapped_findings: Real composition of the Fe-18%Al as-cast alloy (Table 1): nominal 18 at.%; real 17.5-18.0 at.% Al (9.3-9.6 wt.-%); impurities C 40-70 wt.ppm, Si <20-100 wt.ppm, As <70 wt.ppm, Ni <40 wt.ppm.

The yield stress of polycrystalline as-cast Fe-Al alloys increases linearly with Al content up to 18 at.% with a hardening coefficient of about 2.2 GPa (Fig. 3 and Fig. 5a,b), which is not sensitive to deformation rate or temperature; the interpolating straight lines in Fig. 3 indicate a yield stress increase of 21 and 23 MPa per unit % Al at the higher (10^-2 s^-1) and lower (10^-4 s^-1) compression rates, respectively.

The approximately 2.2 GPa hardening coefficient of the polycrystalline as-cast alloys contrasts with the ~1 GPa reported for monocrystals (single-slip) and ~1.8 GPa reported by Morgand et al. for polycrystals; the difference is attributed to alloy preparation (as-cast polycrystals vs annealed monocrystals) and slip mode (multiple vs single slip).

Deformation twinning was observed for the Fe-18%Al as-cast alloy at both compression rates at room temperature; at -100 °C twinning occurred above 14% Al in all specimens and occasionally for 11-14% Al.

Exceptional finding: the studied alloys show only minor effects of short-range ordering and no significant dependence of hardness on heat treatment (hardness data were obtained on Fe-16%Al monocrystals, not on this Fe-18% as-cast alloy).
Brittle fracture without prior necking occurs at room temperature for the as-cast alloy at 18 at.% Al (transition range 15-18 at.% Al at RT; 12-14 at.% Al at -100 °C).
